Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilvawv. dilg_gov.ph D!LG OPINION No. LØ— 02 OCT 2017 MS. CECLIA L. ATIENZA President Liga ng mga Cooperative Development Officers (LCDOP) Dear LDCOP Pres. Atienza: s. 20-11 This has reference to your letter dated 24 October 2016, addressed to His Excellency President Rodrigo R. Duterte, requesting to have local government units (LGUs) be deputized as the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA) local counterpart. Hereunder are this Department's comments and recommendation. Appointment of a Cooperatives Officer It must be emphasized that the appointment of a cooperatives officer in the local government units (LGUs) is optional on the part of the province and city only. Item No. 1 of the proposed Executive Order (EO) provides that the President of the Philippines may deputize LGUs as local counterparts of the CDA on cooperative program formulation and implementation at the "Provincial, City and Municipal levels". Said item would run counter with Sections 454 (b), 463 (b) and 487 (a) of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" or LGC, provide the following: Section 454. Officials of the City Government. (b) In addition thereto, the city mayor may appoint a city architect, a city information officer, a city agriculturist, a city population officer, a city en vironment and natural resources officer, and a city cooperatives officer. Section 463. Officials of the Provincial Government.

(b) In addition thereto, the governor may appoint a provincial population officer, a provincial natural resources and environment officer, a provincial cooperative officer, a provincial architect, and a provincial information officer. Section 487. Qualifications, Powers and Duties. (a) The appointment of the cooperatives officer is optional for the provincial and city governments. Further, Sections 2 and 4, Article X of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, provide that LGUs enjoy local autonomy and the President of the Philippines only exercises general supervision over local governments; thus, these LGUs determine what is best for their growth and development without undue interference or dictation from the central government. The Executive Department may only check whether local governments or their officials were performing their duties as provided by the fundamental law and by statutes. It cannot interfere with local governments, so long as they act within the scope of their authority. 1 However, it must be noted that under Section 443 (c) (2) of the LGC, it provides that the sangguniang bayan may "create such other offices as may be necessary to carry out the purposes of the municipal government". Thus, it is possible for a municipality to create an office that would handle affairs concerning cooperatives operating within its territorial jurisdiction. As the appointment of a cooperatives officer is optional on the part of provincial and city governments, it is respectfully recommended that the comments and recommendations of the League of Provinces in the Philippines (LPP) and the League of Cities in the Philippines (LCP) be solicited. Tawe vs. Santos, G.R. No. 90336, 12 August 1991, 200 SCRA 512.

Deputization ofLGUs as CDA local counterparts on matters relative to and cooperative promotion development at local levels Likewise, it is also recommended that the subject matter herein be referred also to the Cooperatives Development Authority (CDA) as the same is within its competence and mandate. Section 3 (c) and (d) Of RA No. 6939, otherwise known as the "Cooperative Development Authority Act" , provides for the following, to wit: Section 3. Powers, Functions and Responsibilities. — The Authority shall have the following powers, functions and responsibilities: (c) Support the voluntary organization and consensual development ofactivities that promote cooperative movements and provide assistance towards upgrading managerial and technical expertise upon request of the cooperatives concerned; (d) Coordinate the efforts of the local government units and the private sector in promotion, organization, and development of cooperatives; We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. V truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecreta Dlls-o S 28-0 201 Legal/01m DIR. JAIME LI.AGUNO MABILINA Presidential Action Center Office of the President Malacanang, Manila DIR. MANUEL Q. GOTIS, CESO 111 Bureau Of Local Government Supervision (BLGS)
